source.title: Off-Target Effects of Response-Style Alignment in a Korean 27B Language Model

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports effects on abstention in ambiguous Korean social-bias questions and on disclosure emission, not refusal or harmful-request compliance. It explicitly distinguishes its outcomes from refusal behaviour; it does not test the claim versions’ specified behaviours.
record.gate_note: The paper cites work on fine-tuning and safety, but its own evaluations use KoBBQ abstention and investment-disclosure detectors. Those are related but different constructs from complying with harmful user requests. The KoBBQ findings below are recorded as related findings, not evidence for or against V1–V7. The paper does not measure per-token KL, compliant-prefix or suffix attacks, decoding changes as a safety bypass, safety-localized parameters, or deepened safety training.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes Qwen3.8-27B on benign Korean response-style targets, then measures KoBBQ ambiguous-item answer rate and detector-identified financial disclosure. It never measures compliance with harmful requests, per-token KL, prefill, suffix or decoding attacks, safety-localized parameters, or deepened safety training. It cites Qi et al. and casts its style stage as 'the benign fine-tune', but says what moves is not a refusal behaviour. Its results therefore measure related but different constructs: social-bias abstention and disclosure emission.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. Style post-training changed KoBBQ abstention and detector-identified disclosure, carried mainly by answer propensity and response length. The authors explicitly say they do not identify latent preference changes or calibrated regulatory compliance. The distinction from refusal behaviour is made in their related-work framing rather than in the conclusion itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Korean response-style SFT, KoBBQ-targeted safety DPO, and disclosure distillation; it does not reproduce the harmful-example fine-tuning or token-distribution measurements in the claim’s cited sources.
record.method_sensitivity: KoBBQ answer-rate changes depend on target form and show substantial variation across seeds; the hedge-preserving arm is highly unstable. Disclosure-detector agreement varies by checkpoint. Assigned response length changes detector-measured disclosure.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign style-target SFT nudged the ambiguous KoBBQ answer rate up (+0.46 to +1.34 pp across 3 seeds; only seed 1's CI excludes zero). Neutral raw-response targets lowered it (−1.39 to −1.60 pp). Length-matched and hedge-preserving controls landed in between or were unstable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The form of a benign fine-tuning target can shift abstention on ambiguous social-bias questions. This is distinct from harmful-request refusal.

fits_no_version.finding: Style SFT cut detector-identified required financial disclosure by about 22 pp. Most of that gap is reproduced by assigning response length directly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign style fine-tuning can reduce emission of required safety-like disclosure language, largely through verbosity.

record.problems: Evidence is from one model and one language; training arms have three seeds or fewer, and the paper says its control design does not identify the responsible target feature. The training corpus is not released. The paper also reports unresolved KoBBQ provenance and, for disclosure measurements, unverified endpoint identity; these do not turn its outcomes into harmful-request safety measurements.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows retained for the disclosure detector, response-length assignment, option-position sensitivity, or sequential repair pipeline: those outcomes do not measure the harmful-request compliance or token-localized safety behaviours specified by V1–V7.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning data and no harmful-request compliance or refusal outcome.
Benign style SFT is run, but harmful-request compliance is never measured. Only KoBBQ abstention and disclosure emission are measured.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL on harmful prompts.
No prefilled compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change attack on refusal.
LoRA rank 8 is used only as a training tool. There is no test of whether safety sits in a few weights or ranks.
No analysis of why safety alignment is shallow.

The KoBBQ-targeted safety DPO is a bias-abstention repair, not training that spreads harmful-request refusal beyond the first tokens. Its durability against harmful fine-tuning or attacks is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The record's gate is sound. All rows correctly carry versions ['none'], and their cannot_determine states are acceptable for unlinked rows. The disclosure, option-position and pipeline-order results also bear on no version, so leaving them out as rows is acceptable. The safety DPO stage targets KoBBQ bias abstention, not harmful-request refusal, so it does not engage V7.

versions.untested_parts: No harmful-request prompts or harmful fine-tuning examples; no harmful-compliance or refusal outcome.
No measurement of harmful-request compliance after ordinary or carefully chosen benign fine-tuning.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement on harmful prompts.
No compliant opening, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test of harmful-request refusal.
LoRA is used for training, but the study does not test whether safety behaviour is localized in weights or ranks.
The study does not test why safety behaviour is shallow or whether safety data or objectives produce shallowness.
No training designed to deepen harmful-request safety or test whether such deepening holds up.
